facts.statement: Philip D. Mannion and Alejandro Otero first described and named the genus Elaltitan in 2012.
facts.quote: Elaltitan was first described and named by Philip D. Mannion and Alejandro Otero in 2012

facts.statement: The species name lilloi honors Miguel Lillo for his contributions to natural sciences in Tucumán.
facts.quote: The specific name, lilloi, honors Miguel Lillo, for his contribution and legacy to natural sciences in Tucumán

facts.statement: The genus Elaltitan contains only one known species, Elaltitan lilloi.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Elaltitan lilloi

facts.statement: Fossils of Elaltitan are found in the Late Cretaceous (mid Cenomanian to Turonian stages) of Chubut Province, southern Argentina.
facts.quote: known from the Late Cretaceous (mid Cenomanian to Turonian stage) of Chubut Province, southern Argentina

facts.statement: Elaltitan is the first titanosaur skeleton known to preserve an associated calcaneum.
facts.quote: Elaltitan is the first titanosaur skeleton to preserve an associated calcaneum

facts.statement: The holotype specimen dates to the middle Cenomanian to Turonian stage, approximately 96.5 to 89.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: It came from the lower member of the Bajo Barreal Formation, dating to the middle Cenomanian to the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous period, about 96.5-89.3 million years ago

facts.statement: The holotype was collected by an expedition led by José Fernando Bonaparte for the Fundación Miguel Lillo and the Universidad Nacional de Tucumán.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was collected by an expedition of the Fundación Miguel Lillo and the Universidad Nacional de Tucumán, led by José Fernando Bonaparte

facts.statement: Elaltitan is considered one of the largest sauropods ever to have existed.
facts.quote: This makes it one of the largest known sauropods ever to have existed

facts.statement: Estimates of Elaltitan's weight have varied, ranging from 35.4 tonnes in 2018 to 42.8 tonnes in 2014.
facts.quote: Its weight has been estimated at 42.8 t in 2014, and at 35.4 t in 2018

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Molina-Perez and Larramendi estimated Elaltitan's size at 20 meters (66 ft) and 23 tonnes.
facts.quote: However, in 2020 Molina-Perez and Larramendi gave a smaller size of 20 meters (66 ft) and 23 tonnes (25.35 short tons)

facts.statement: Elaltitan belongs to the parent group Lithostrotia.
Elaltitan is classified within the class Saurischia.
The Paleobi Database records the time range for Elaltitan as the Coniacian stage, from 89.8 to 85.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Coniacian (89.8 to 85.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Before its formal description, the holotype of Elaltitan was originally attributed to Antarctosaurus sp. and later tentatively referred to Argyrosaurus.
facts.quote: The holotype of Elaltitan was originally attributed to Antarctosaurus sp. by Bonaparte & Gasparini (1979), and later tentatively referred to Argyrosaurus by Jaime Powell (1986, 2003)
